fact: The Direction générale du patrimoine de l'État (DGPE) held an intensive course in computing, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence from 7 to 17 October 2025 in Libreville, delivered by DigieWomen School, which GabonReview says trained nearly 300 agents.

On 7 September 2026 the Centre Gabonais de l'Innovation ran an introductory AI-tools session for over forty agents of the Ministry of Communication and Media, ahead of the RCAPE programme planning to train 500 state agents by December 2026.

Gabonactu reports that agents of the Treasury (DGCPT) took a three-day course on digital tools and artificial intelligence at the Centre Gabonais de l'Innovation, after officials of the Communication ministry and the Budget directorate (DGB) took it; no number trained is given.

fact: On 2 March 2026 Gabon's Minister of Digital Economy and Smart Africa signed an MoU to deploy the Smart Africa Digital Academy, with training for public administration staff among its targets, hosted by the Gabonese Centre for Innovation.

Gabonmediatime reports the Ministry of Digital Economy, with UNESCO and two universities, launched the Global Skills Academy campaign on 15 October 2024, offering 2,000 free certified courses, with public service agents among the main targets.
